children.author: pests
children.text:
DeepSeek does. The entire thing is composed on plugins, using a framework called Cordis. Everything is a plugin. All the tools, the models, plan mode, file system access, everything. You can change anything anywhere, even reconfiguring active plugins deep internally. Cordis provides an effect system so everything can be rewound on uninstall time. This is how people run local models or just other major models, just by writing a new plugin to talk to whatever instead of the deepseek api. The agent loop itself is a plugin and can be swapped out.

https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis

DeepSeek Harness allows the user/agent to build its own plug-ins and run them without restart, mostly. Pi and OpenCode were then influenced to do the same in their respective new versions. I don't know which has the better implementation.

children.author: sieve
children.text:
The pricing is opaque for stupid reasons. All the information is actually available for you to calculate your usage exactly.

- You pay $10/mo for Go and get $10 worth of usage per month

- Now, each model they make available has a multiplier from 1.5-8x

- So, the expensive ones like Kimi K3 have a 1.5x multiplier, cheaper ones like DeepSeek 4.1 Flash have 8x

- This gives you usage of $15 and $80 per month respectively

- You can mix and match

- So, you can use 25% of your quota with K3 and 75% with DS41Flash ... usage of $3.75 and $60 respectively

- You divide the two figures by their respective multiplier ... $3.75 / 1.5 and $60 / 8 ... and you end up with $2.5 + $7.5 = $10 which is what you paid

- You should ignore the requests table and go directly to the price/M tokens table where all the actual rates are given

- They control usage at 5h/1w/1mo intervals

- You can use 25% of your monthly quota in a 5h block, 50% in a week, and 100% in a month.

- If you were only using DS41Flash, that is $20m, $40 and $80 worth of usage respectively which is $2.5, $5 and $10 of your subscription figure after accounting for the multipliers.

It would be so much simpler if they credited 1M microdollars per $1 of subscription and quoted the per M token rates for each model in this currency.

But then Claude/Codex/StepFun and all the other subscription services are far more opaque.

children.author: ghrl
children.text:
This is quite confusing, indeed, but the limits are generous and transparent once you understand the concept.

There are two plans, OpenCode Go and Go Plus, for 10$/mo and 40$/mo.

With your plan, you get a specific monthly amount of money you can use, with separate weekly and 5-hour limits to not spend all at once.

The amount of money you can use depends on the model, but the usage percentage adds up regardless. For example, on the Haiku Model, the monthly limit is 15$/mo, as you read from the page. For other models, such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the limit is now 80$/mo (the increased it from 60$ recently).

This might seem odd, but the stated purpose of OpenCode Go is "Low cost coding models for everyone", so the limits on the open models tend to be higher.

The math works like this: You use 5$ no Haiku and 20$ on a 60$ model, then your monthly limit is used 66.6%, meaning 5$ of Haiku or 20$ of a 60$ model remaining.

Another way to view this is as follows: You have 10$ flat usage per month, and the "higher usage on each model" is actually just a discount on the token price. So Haiku is discounted to 10$/15$=66.6%, DeepSeek to 12.5% and so on.

Go Plus just means you get more usage, though the rate is not always 4x.

To answer your remaining questions: The billing is based on the actual provider's api costs, so input/cached/output tokens. I suppose the "requests" number is estimated. The OpenCode TUI and your account website actually show the real session prices, which also helps with an understanding how expensive the agents are on raw (unsubsidized) api pricing. The usage limits are rolling, so there is a 5-hour, a weekly and a monthly limit. The 5h is 20% of the monthly limit, and the weekly is 50% (not sure on the exact numbers).

I would agree that the pricing is confusing, but for the price you get surprisingly much usage, especially on the 60$ models. Give DeepSeek V4.1 a try, you get nearly unlimited usage and it's around Sonnet/Opus level.
